decision: scaffold first: npm, node>=24 running .ts directly, biome, strict tsc, node --test, ci, renovate
why: every later phase benefits from lint, typecheck and test gates existing before features

decision: ran three parallel architect runners (opus, sonnet, haiku) on the hunk-splitting data model and applier
why: the plan format and out-of-order hunk applier are one-way doors; want structurally distinct candidates before committing

decision: synthesized from opus and sonnet candidates: project file content from base plus applied change lines, no patch application at all
why: all hunks come from one diff so they are disjoint in base coordinates; out-of-order assignment cannot misapply, which deletes the fuzz matcher and its failure modes

decision: temporary index plus commit-tree with fixed dates instead of fast-import
why: same determinism, simpler to debug with ordinary git commands

decision: unanswered review comments are warnings, not validation errors
why: a human must still be able to apply a plan they are happy with

decision: mode-only text files get a TextFile with no hunks
why: the mode unit needs the base bytes to write the file; reusing TextFile keeps one projection path

decision: parseDiff also asserts that projecting every change line reproduces the tip blob
why: catches parser bugs at extract time, before a plan exists

decision: git diff runs with --no-abbrev and --no-textconv in addition to the contract flags
why: raw output abbreviates shas without --no-abbrev; textconv would make hunks disagree with blobs

decision: playback mode narrated by browser speech synthesis, narration text authored by the planner as optional plan fields
why: user wants to watch the branch being written with audio; built-in speech keeps it offline with no key or dependency, and putting narration in the plan keeps one source of truth per commit

decision: tree checks (path-conflict, final-mismatch) run only when the line assignment is complete
why: on a broken assignment they only restate unassigned and duplicate issues

decision: plan base mismatch is reported as malformed at $.base, tip mismatch as stale
why: the stale issue carries only the tip; a base mismatch means the plan was written for another merge-base

decision: two commands over one engine: split for the author (applies a branch, comments feed the next plan) and walk for a reviewer (no apply, playback with narration, comments become a markdown code review)
why: user clarified two personas; the projection, plan and review UI are shared, only the apply step and the feedback renderer differ

decision: commit-tree runs with --no-gpg-sign and messages get a trailing newline
why: commit.gpgSign would make SHAs non-deterministic and prompt for a key

decision: writeBranch returns unchanged when the ref already points at the computed head, even if expectedOld differs
why: the ref is already where apply would put it; refusing would break idempotent re-runs

decision: apply defaults --name to <branch>-split
why: never rewrites the user's branch unless asked; --name <branch> --force is safe because the final tree equals the checked-out tip

decision: issues and commit lists print 0-based commit indices
why: matches the $.commits[i] JSON paths the planner edits

decision: splitting is per change line, not per file or hunk; a plan takes any subset of a hunk's lines and orders lines of one file across commits freely
why: the user asked that lines move to an earlier commit when the story needs it; the projection engine already makes any line subset well-defined
result: confirmed, limit: no intermediate states absent from base or tip

decision: narration lives in the plan, on commits and on unit refs
why: one planner call produces both the commit order and the voice-over, and the narration stays bound to the exact units it describes
evidence: src/plan.ts parsePlanFile, src/anthropic.ts PLAN_SCHEMA, docs/DESIGN.md Reviewer mode and playback

decision: ran both flows by hand on the fixture: split (plan with a split hunk, check caught planted errors, apply proved the tree hash, v2 answered both comments) and walk (narrated plan, walk server, comment, code review digest)
why: prove it works on the real artifact, not the tests alone; the UI itself could not be opened because no browser is available on this machine
result: VERIFIED except the browser UI, INCONCLUSIVE there

decision: apply never writes the session's branch or any branch checked out in a worktree, --force included; supersedes the 04:27 entry that allowed --name <branch> --force
why: the user wants new commits on a new branch so the original is never at risk; update-ref on a checked-out branch desynchronises that worktree's index and files

decision: one review server per user that hosts many sessions; later review or walk calls register with it instead of starting another; busy port is probed for our own server first, otherwise a free port is chosen; uninstall mirrors install
why: user asked for a single server instance that still serves multiple repos and worktrees, graceful port handling, and easy uninstall

decision: apply, review and walk take <session>/lock; the lock is written whole to a temp file and link(2)ed into place, which fails on EEXIST like open(wx); a dead pid's lock is taken over; release removes the lock only if its token is ours
why: two agents on one session would otherwise race on freeze, applied.json and reviews/vN; link keeps a reader from seeing a half-written lock, which wx followed by write cannot; two processes breaking the same stale lock in the same instant can still both proceed

decision: clean removes sessions whose branch is gone, review drafts at or below the latest finished review version, locks and *.<pid>.*.tmp files of dead pids, and object quarantines of dead applies; plan versions are kept; --all removes .follow-me/ and refuses while a live process holds a session
why: a draft at or below the latest review can never be resumed because a version is reviewed once; temp names carry the pid so a live writer's file is never taken

decision: one review server per user: server.json in FOLLOW_ME_HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME/follow-me or ~/.local/state/follow-me, claimed by link like the session lock; a registry keyed by SessionId (12 hex of sha256 over the session dir) serves /s/<id>/; review and walk register with a live server or become it (foreground, or --detach as follow-me server run); the server takes the session lock over by token from the CLI; it exits 30s after its last session and removes server.json; supersedes the 06:36 plan
why: user asked for a single server instance that still handles many workstreams; a dir-derived id makes re-registering idempotent; taking the lock by token leaves no gap between CLI release and server acquire; the idle window lets back-to-back reviews reuse one server
evidence: src/server.ts startServer, src/host.ts, test/cli.test.ts two sessions share one server

decision: port handling: a --port held by our own server (GET /api/health answers app follow-me) means attach; held by anything else, listen on a free port and print 'port N is in use by another program, using M'; server stop only signals a pid that answers as ours on the recorded port
why: user asked that a taken port be handled gracefully; probing health rather than trusting the pid tells our server from a stranger and keeps a reused pid from being killed
evidence: src/host.ts startOrAttach and stopServer, test/cli.test.ts busy port tests

decision: linux-only test failures were EPIPE on git's stdin when git exited before reading it (optional ref lookups); handled on the stdin stream, ci green
why: the real git error already arrives through the exec callback, the pipe write failure was noise that only linux raised

decision: mermaid diagrams as a separate diagram field per commit and unit, rendered in a side panel that follows playback, mermaid bundled and served locally
why: user wants the agent to explain with diagrams during a walk; narration stays plain text because it is spoken; no cdn keeps the page offline

decision: apply signs split commits when git config --type=bool commit.gpgsign is true, --sign/--no-sign override; writeBranch passes -S or --no-gpg-sign explicitly; applied.json gains plan hash and signed, and apply skips the write and prints unchanged when version, hash, branch, signed and the branch head all match the record; supersedes the 04:23 --no-gpg-sign row
why: user needs signing preserved when recommitting; commit-tree is plumbing and ignores commit.gpgsign (git 2.9.1+), so not countermanding it would never sign; openpgp, x509 and ecdsa signatures differ per run so SHA equality cannot mean unchanged, while ed25519 is deterministic and still hits the SHA path
evidence: test/cli.test.ts ed25519 and ecdsa signing tests, git verify-commit on every split commit; disabling the record check fails the ecdsa test

decision: walk reviews and their autosaved drafts live in reviews/walk/vN.json (and vN.draft.json), chosen by host.ts loadHosted passing session.reviewsDir(mode) as Loaded.reviewsDir; reviews/vN.json stays the split slot, lastReview reads split only, older walk reviews in reviews/vN.json still count as walk reviews; asked for reviews/vN.walk.json
why: server.ts names both the review file and its draft from reviewsDir and the version, so a per-mode directory separates both without editing server.ts; a vN.walk.json name would still share vN.draft.json with a split review of the same plan
evidence: test/cli.test.ts walk after a split review of v1, feedback and feedback --walk print only their own comments; test/session.test.ts reviews and walkReviews
result: chosen; rename to vN.walk.json needs server.ts to take the file names from Loaded

decision: live loop: follow-me watch blocks until new comments, apply swaps the hosted plan version in place, the page re-renders on a server event and shows answers inline; ending the review stays optional
why: user does not want to close and reopen the server between plan versions; the server already hosts sessions and autosaves comments, so the missing pieces are a wait command, in-place version swap and page events
result: planned after the playback rebuild and the question loop

decision: the agent talks to the server api, not files: long-poll events endpoint with a sequence number, reply endpoint for explanations with optional mermaid, in-place version swap on apply; files remain the durable record written on end
why: user wants the loop to feel interactive; polling files is slow and racy, the server already owns the session state
result: planned, same slice as the live loop

decision: syntax highlighting in the review page from a locally served highlighter, language by file extension, diff state as background tint under token colours
why: user asked for highlighting while reviewing; a cdn would break the offline page

decision: every sliced commit must parse: prompt rule to keep files syntactically whole, a per-extension syntax gate in check and apply over projected files, --syntax override and --allow-syntax-errors escape
why: user wants intermediate commits syntactically correct even if they do not build; the projection makes each commit's file content available to parse without a checkout
result: planned after the live loop lands

decision: playback is the chunk stepper (Design B with C's context rules); a say step lasts the later of its reading time and speech end plus tail, for intros and chunks alike
why: the review lets a chunk reveal at speech end; taking the later of the two keeps a card readable when speech outruns reading at 1.5x and 2x, and one rule is simpler than two
evidence: test/playback.test.ts literal schedule at 1x and 2x; eight-commit fixture plays in 111.9s with speech at 1x (silent floor 108.5s), was 15.6s

decision: mermaid 12.2.0 exact-pinned; /vendor/mermaid.mjs serves dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs and /vendor/chunks/mermaid.esm.min/<name>.mjs its chunks, names checked by regex; the page imports it dynamically only when a plan has a diagram and inserts its svg under securityLevel strict
why: the ESM build is split into about 200 chunks imported by relative path, so a single file cannot be served; dynamic import keeps diagram-free plans from loading it; strict mode has mermaid sanitize its own svg
evidence: src/server.test.ts fetches the entry and a chunk it imports; headless Chrome shows no /vendor request on a commit without a diagram

decision: gutter shows base and tip line numbers computed in the UI from hunk oldStart and earlier hunks of the file; comments display tip lines and removed lines by old number; anchors keep change indices
why: the review asked for real numbers without moving the comment wire format; the UI already has every hunk, so the server state needs nothing new
evidence: test/playback.test.ts lineNumbers and describeLines; fixture comment on mul's guards reads lines 14-15, matching git show feature:src/lib.js

decision: under 900px the rail hides titles visually (clip) rather than with display none, and its floating tooltip is described by aria-describedby; the index page's session age comes from an in-memory openedAt so HostedSummary and /api/sessions are unchanged
why: display none would drop the title from each row's accessible name; keeping age out of the summary avoids a wire change host.ts would have to parse
evidence: headless Chrome at 800px: row name keeps the title, tooltip shows on focus; server test asserts the index row and empty state

decision: dogfood: a naive one-commit-per-file planner so ci can run extract, check, apply and the proof on follow-me's own last commits; plus a hand-planned split of a real slice walked in the browser
why: user asked to dogfood on our own commits; real sources exercise the syntax gate and the projection better than the fixture

decision: record a playback gif for the readme after the chunk-stepper lands, via the preview browser recording and ffmpeg
why: user asked for a gif on github; recording before the pacing fix would show the wrong thing

decision: interactive loop: in-memory append-only event log per hosted session (long-poll and SSE), replies on comments, in-place version swap through the loader under the server's own lock, one renderReport for feedback, report and vN.md; check and apply validate against the open review's autosave
why: the owner wants agent and page to talk live without reopening the server; files stay the durable record; responses to comments that exist only on the open page must validate
evidence: server.test.ts events replies swap stream; cli.test.ts watch reply report apply swap; plan.test.ts concerns answers

decision: drove the interactive loop on the real server in the browser: question from the page reached watch --follow in under a second, two agent replies with a mermaid diagram appeared live, concern kept, end wrote the consolidated report with both voices
why: prove it works on the real artifact after merging the two halves built against a pinned contract

decision: syntax gate by extension table: node --check for js, module.stripTypeScriptTypes in a child node for ts (node --check and --experimental-strip-types --check both reject valid ts, typescript 7 has no transpileModule), JSON.parse, sh/bash -n, py_compile; jsx tsx yaml and the rest skipped and counted; a file failing at the tip is the tip's own state and is not checked earlier; apply refuses unless --allow-syntax-errors
why: owner: sliced commits must stay syntactically correct but need not pass tests; blaming a split for a tip that does not parse would be wrong
evidence: node --check on ok.ts exits 1; stripTypeScriptTypes accepts it and rejects a missing brace; test/syntax.test.ts; scripts/dogfood.sh
result: chosen; open: yaml and jsx have no parser, tip failures warn instead of blocking, naive planner on a file-to-directory swap is untested

decision: conversation wire (server and CLI half): Anchor.hunk.offsets, Comment.author and Comment.diagram, follow-me explain, ConcernDecision.decidedAt; offsets validated only against body length; --lines of explain are change lines, offsets derived; agent threads need no response and reach the report only after a reviewer reply
why: ux-review section 8: any-line selection needs a wire that names context rows, and the agent must be able to open a thread; the consistency check of changes against offsets would reject a page that disagrees on ownership, so it is left to the page
evidence: server.test.ts offsets author decidedAt; rows.test.ts quoting; cli.test.ts explain
result: chosen; open: changes not cross-checked with offsets, explain cannot pick context rows, Comment.diagram is beyond section 8

decision: drove the conversation design on the real server: explain thread with a diagram in the timeline, a comment on a context line reached watch as src/lib.js:6 with the picked row marked
why: prove the merged halves work together, not only against stubs

decision: cut playback, speech, the player and the side column; the product is split into sequential commits plus inline review, flag, ask, answer, with diagrams full-width inline
why: user tried the page and found the player impractical and the layout clunky; subtract before adding

decision: the review's output must port to gitlab or github: comments keep original-branch path and line, report --json emits discussion-ready items, the agent posts them through glab or gh from its harness; follow-me never holds credentials
why: user: usage is always from a harness, review locally, ask, understand, consolidate, then port comments to the merge request

decision: follow-me never calls a model: removed the Anthropic planner, @anthropic-ai/sdk, --model and the ANTHROPIC_* handling; the coding agent writes draft.json from follow-me prompt, and plan keeps only --naive
why: the owner will never support API keys directly; a harness already has a model and credentials, and a second planner path duplicated the first and needed network in tests
evidence: commit refactor(cli)!: drop the Anthropic planner; npm run check green

decision: rebuild the page with vite, react, tailwind and shadcn; markdown replies via marked plus dompurify with mermaid fences; lightbox zoom on diagrams; server serves ui/dist
why: user asked for shadcn so the components are polished out of the box, markdown replies and tap-to-zoom; the cut list removes most of the vanilla page anyway

decision: held flags, exclusions and report --json: flags are pending until api/submit and hidden from the agent through audience=agent on the event log; exclusions are stored as lists of ids and default to none (questions are not excluded by the server); the JSON item carries no id and the merge request head is checked against follow-me status
why: the owner wants one explicit send step and a hand-off to glab or gh with no token in follow-me; filtering at read time keeps the page's log whole and the CLI stateless
evidence: server.test.ts held flags and exclusions; rows.test.ts report items; prompt.test.ts
result: chosen; open: questions are excluded by default only if the page posts it

decision: bare follow-me is the one agent entry: idempotent, returns on every call, long-polls 60s from a cursor.json keyed by session id and openedAt; mode comes from applied.json, else from whether user.email authored every commit; review/walk/feedback and the step commands stay but leave the default help; the skill installs itself on every run
why: the owner's agent did not know it could listen and the human should type nothing; one command with a next: line removes the choices
evidence: test/cli.test.ts no-command states test and reviewer-mode test
result: chosen; open: the authorship heuristic can misjudge a squashed or rebased branch, hence --author and --reviewer

decision: ran the one-command flow on a fixture: skill self-installed, prompt handoff, apply with proof, page launched; a context-line question from the rebuilt page reached follow-me --wait and a markdown reply with a mermaid fence rendered inline
why: prove the merged rebuild on the real server before tagging

decision: comments reach the agent immediately, no held flags; after the agent commits a fix on the original branch, follow-me re-splits keeping unchanged hunk assignments, applies the next version and swaps it into the open page with threads carried over and marked changed
why: user expects a live update after asking for a code change in a comment

decision: a moved tip evolves the session: evolvePlan keeps refs whose unit id survives, drops vanished ones and empty commits, lists added units; the old diff comes from the latest plan's base and tip; the hosted page swaps and api/state.carried places each previous comment on the new diff (same id unchanged, else nearest hunk on the path by tip line, changed: true); replies to previous comments are stored as earlierReplies in the current version's review because finished reviews are written once; --wait defaults to 90s, capped at 300
why: the owner wants a live update after asking for a change in a comment, and the agent stopped after one call; recomputing everything from disk and git keeps every call idempotent
evidence: test/evolve.test.ts; src/server.test.ts carried threads; test/cli.test.ts moved-branch and swap tests
result: chosen; open: newLine is a heuristic (same text, else clamped old line) and the report of the new version does not list earlierReplies

decision: reconnect without loss: a session's log starts with a replay of its saved comments and replies in createdAt order; cursor.json keeps seq for one log plus the ids of every comment and reply read; follow-me and watch restart a dead server on the port in server.json and re-register from disk
why: the agent must survive a server restart, and an open page can only follow a server on the same origin
evidence: test/cli.test.ts killed-server test; src/server.test.ts replay test
result: chosen; open: a live but hung server is not replaced, and replayed comment-updated or concern events are not part of the replay

decision: drove the live loop on the real server: a flag reached follow-me at once, the agent committed a fix, follow-me evolved the plan, applied v2 with proof and swapped the page; the thread was carried with a changed chip and a what-changed diff; the badge jumped to it; SIGKILL then follow-me restarted the server on the same port with the thread and reply intact
why: prove the whole round trip, which also surfaced the earlier-review validation bug fixed in ed95c13

decision: what the agent reads: fixed instructions move to the skill (Writing the draft; porting.md read on demand), prompt.md keeps session data and one line naming the section; the re-plan prompt sends bodies only for new units; digests send refs plus a quote capped at 6 rows of 160 chars for unseen comments; follow-me show expands h_, c_, k_ and path:line@n; ordering is top-down
why: the owner asked for token savings without losing quality; the prompts were 97% of a real session and the re-plan resent the whole dump
evidence: scripts/measure-tokens.ts; docs/token-budget.md (fixture 24314 to 18633 bytes, real branch 474939 to 247413); blind sonnet runs on 6d7c562 and cae6178: same calls, no fix rounds, correct answer, final reads top-down; test/skill.test.ts holds every moved rule
result: chosen; open: re-plan and show not covered by a blind run; the report of a swapped version still omits earlier comments

decision: one review spans every version swapped into the open page: at each swap the server carries what the session already carried plus the old version's comments onto the new diff (carrySession; changed is sticky, since names the last version whose code matched), and kept concerns the next plan lost with their decision (carryConcerns); decisions, resolutions and exclusions move into the new view; reviews/vN.draft.json and vN.json store carried as refs { version, comment, since, placement } plus carriedConcerns whole, saved at the swap; the loader and report read refs back from the version files (sessionComments); the report folds them onto the final tip with 'the code changed after vN' or 'the code is gone after vN'; report items gain id and an optional changed { since, gone }
why: the reviewer answers the code writer once, at the end, and the report of a swapped version dropped everything said before the swap; the root cause was that a swap carried only the previous version's own comments, so v1 was lost at the second swap
evidence: test/cli.test.ts swapped-twice test (literal report JSON from the server and from disk, markdown once each, server killed between swaps); test/evolve.test.ts second-swap test; ui Handoff carried-item test
result: chosen; closes the open notes of rows 54 and 57 (the report of a swapped version omits earlier comments and earlierReplies); open: seeded decisions, resolutions and exclusions are repeated in each later version's file as state, and a fresh open after an ended review still shows the previous review's threads for context without reporting them

decision: go to definition: one pattern table per language in src/definition.ts, each written in the subset JS regexes and POSIX ERE share, so the same text is git grep's -e over the tip commit and the per-extension filter; a JS-only reject drops statements like return parse(s); names are ASCII identifiers (else 400); commit in a Candidate is 0-based like ProjectedCommit.index; the server sends preview empty for an in-plan hit because the page reads its hunk, while show prints it; matches are cached per name in the hosted view, which a swap replaces; commit sections are optional and serialize only when present
why: the page owner jumps or peeks on Cmd-click and the agent needs the same answer without reading the working tree, which is not the tip; one table cannot drift between the grep and the filter
evidence: test/definition.test.ts (later-commit definition, context row, previews, ranking, 400, swap, eight languages with call sites excluded); test/cli.test.ts show <name>; test/plan.test.ts sections; measure-tokens skill 11016 to 11350
result: chosen; open: non-ASCII identifiers are refused; multi-line signatures and arrow-function class fields are not found; patterns are verified on Apple git 2.54 only

decision: coverage while reading, server and CLI half: follow-me coverage parses lcov (TN SF DA BRDA, other records skipped, bad lines named) into coverage.json at the tip; SF paths resolve against cwd then the root, symlinks resolved, and paths outside the repo or absent from the tip tree are dropped rather than refused; the tip check is git diff --name-only <tip> over covered paths; a plain run replaces everything and its named TN blocks become tests, a --test run adds one test and folds hits in by max; GET api/coverage reads the file from disk each time and adds stale, the covered paths changed between coverage.tip and the hosted tip (all when that commit is gone); POST api/coverage emits { type: coverage, tip, takenAt } and is not news for the agent; the report counts only non-stale files, adds one coverage line per file heading and covered on flags and kept concerns over executable added rows
why: the reviewer asked what code paths are covered as they read; coverage is evidence only from a real run, and a moved tip is the only thing that invalidates it, so plan swaps must not
evidence: test/coverage.test.ts (parse, malformed lines, relativization, accumulation, dirty refusal, event on a hosted page, no stale after a same-tip re-plan, lib.js stale after a commit, report via the server); src/server.test.ts api/coverage 404, served, restarted server; src/prompt.test.ts report lines; measure-tokens fixture 20227 to 20630 bytes
result: chosen; open: hit counts from --test runs alone are a lower bound (max, not sum); the entry does not tell the agent to re-run coverage after a tip move, the skill does; lcov paths with backslashes (Windows) are not handled; covered is set on concerns as well as flags

decision: offers and state maps, server and CLI half: offers { kind, label } on commits and unit refs; o_ ids over unit (empty for a commit) and label so reordering keeps them; check refuses >1 per commit and >3 per plan; accepting is a reviewer question with offer (400 unknown, already accepted in this review incl. carried, or dismissed; PUT cannot change it); POST api/offers/<id>/dismiss stores dismissedOffers in draft and review, carried whole across swaps, sent in api/state, event offer-dismissed, not news; the digest prints one fixed line per accepted offer and next: names the oldest unanswered one; reply may be only a diagram; Reply.map checked for shape and names by the server and against the tip by reply --map, every bad entry named; coverage --reset and preview on tests outside the branch
why: the reviewer wants a picture only when it saves reading, and a state machine view needs code locations the page can derive coverage over; one source of truth for 'never offered again' is the comments and dismissedOffers the page already reads
evidence: test/plan.test.ts (ids stable across reorder, round trip, plain hash, malformed kind and label, limits, repeat); src/server.test.ts (accept, its 400s, dismiss 404/400/idempotent, event, draft and review, swap carries both, map stored and carried); test/cli.test.ts (watch and entry literal lines, next: until replied, map errors for unknown path, past-end lines, unknown transition state, undrawn state, show); test/coverage.test.ts (--reset, preview); measure-tokens skill 11647 to 12686
result: chosen; open: commit offers share a place, so two commits cannot offer the same label; the server does not check map paths against the tip (only the CLI does); the comment's anchor is not checked against the offer's place; definition previews are still latin1 while test previews are UTF-8; not verified in a browser against the page

decision: refs in reply and explain: a code span is a ref when it is wholly path:a[-b][@n|@base] and the path has a letter and a / or a dot (so 10:30, localhost:3000 and 127.0.0.1:80 stay code; an extensionless top-level file like Makefile:3 does not count); the CLI parses and resolves them, like --map, and posts refs; the server only parses their shape; CodeRef stores n, the written path/start/end/at, up to 8 quoted lines (UTF-8), the tip sha it was resolved on, and lines (tip lines) and old (base lines the branch removes); an @n ref is converted to tip lines at post time by replaying the plan's first n commits over the diff, so a new plan version needs no re-resolution; explain stores refs on the agent's Comment since it has no Reply; refs only on agent words
why: 11.6 is silent on the false-positive rule, on who resolves, and on how @n survives a re-plan; tip lines are the coordinate the page already numbers rows by
evidence: test/refs.test.ts (spans, fences, escapes, dedupe, tip/commit/base/removed resolution, every refusal at once, unchanged file); test/cli.test.ts reply/explain store refs, no-ref reply unchanged, show ranges
result: chosen; open: a moved tip makes every ref stale rather than re-finding the quote; refs in a reviewer's reply are refused; mixed ranges spanning removed and kept lines store both spans

decision: ref chips on the page: marked renders a ref code span as an empty data-ref placeholder and React portals a live chip into it; a ref lands in the last commit that owns any of its lines (earlier lines read as context there), context rows go to the first commit taking the unit, rows that commit does not show stay with their owner; tint, gutter badge and bar are data attributes painted on the row elements while the reply block is hovered or focused, so hunks never re-render; a chip jump pushes one departure labelled 'Back to the reply' through a new depart() on the go-to context and scrolls the first row to 30% with row-flash; the peek is the definition Peek component in a popover owned by the chip, opened on hover only for off-screen code and on click for code outside the branch or stale refs, without taking focus; a ref is stale exactly when its tip differs from the session tip; a Viewed commit opens through reveal and stays open after, as x and the definition jump leave it
why: 11.6 asks for tint only while hovered and for the existing peek; painting the DOM keeps hover cheap on long pages; one owner of the hover popover avoids fighting the definition layer's focus handling
evidence: ui/src/lib/refs.test.ts (placement, ranges over two commits, removed rows, off, stale, labels, span lookup); ui/src/components/Refs.test.tsx (chips, tint and badge, strong on chip hover, jump into a Viewed later commit and Alt+Left back, off-branch peek, stale peek, carried thread, off-screen hover peek); ui/src/lib/history.test.ts label
result: chosen; open: the Viewed commit is not collapsed again; a ref spanning hunks in two commits tints both; own commit of a carried thread is its old anchor's

decision: walkthrough stepping: a reply with 2+ refs is a walkthrough; Enter on its focusable block starts at step 1 and clicking any chip starts at that chip's step; the start pushes one departure (Back to the reply) and Back ending below that depth ends the walkthrough; . and , clamp at the ends rather than wrap; Esc ends it and clears the tints but keeps the one departure so Back still returns; a step whose code is off the page or stale opens its quote in a popover above the bar; the bar is sticky at the bottom of the code column after the last commit; captions come from marked's tokens of the list item that first holds each ref, with ref spans dropped and inline code kept as text; a one-ref reply has no bar, its chip just jumps
why: 11.6 says Back is one hop and Alt+Left returns from anywhere in the walkthrough; a walkthrough left open after Back would step without a way back
evidence: ui/src/components/Refs.test.tsx (Enter, ., clamp, ,, quote above the bar, Esc, chip start in a Viewed commit, Previous step button, Alt+Left ends it at the reply, one-ref reply); ui/src/lib/refs.test.ts captions
result: chosen; open: the step bar does not follow the walkthrough's reply if the plan swaps mid-walk

decision: teaching refs: one sentence in the skill's reply step (write path:a-b or path:a-b@3 in backticks; a numbered list with one per item becomes a walkthrough) and the show line's grammar moved to path:a-b; the full help's reply entry names it; the next: lines stay unchanged because they repeat on every batch while the skill is read once
why: the token budget counts every next: line per call; the agent already writes path:line, so one sentence and a refusal that lists every bad ref are enough to steer it
evidence: node scripts/measure-tokens.ts: skill 12686 to 12867 bytes (+181), totals 21753 to 21934 (fixture) and 252370 to 252551 (real), no other step moved; docs/token-budget.md row j
result: chosen; open: no blind-agent quality gate run for refs
